title: dedicated: improve fleet autoscaler burst controls and utilization reporting (v15)
author: Ethan Cole
description:
Motivation: Dedicated fleets can experience short peak load bursts that should be allowed (up to a configurable budget) without triggering aggressive scale-outs. At the same time, utilization reporting was regressing in edge cases where KV-cache heavy workloads artificially inflated per-GPU token accounting. This PR introduces burst controls to the fleet autoscaler and fixes utilization accounting for KV-cache dominated request patterns, adds end-to-end tests, and updates the docs and console telemetry.

What this PR does: 1) Autoscaler: adds configurable burst_budget_pct and burst_cooldown_s knobs; autoscaler will allow transient headroom up to burst_budget_pct of fleet capacity, and then ramp down according to burst_cooldown_s before considering scale-in decisions. 2) Throughput guarantees: clarifies how reserved capacity and burst budget interact in the scheduler; requests are now tagged with budget_consume keys so we can attribute token use to burst vs steady-state. 3) Utilization reporting: fixes per-GPU utilization accounting to exclude KV-cache-only requests from inflating compute utilization and adds a correction factor for shortening sequences from prefix-cached requests. 4) Telemetry: exposes new metrics (fleet.burst_budget_used_pct, fleet.burst_cooldown_remaining_s, gpu.util_kv_cache_corrected_pct) and corresponding console graph panels. 5) Tests & Docs: adds integration tests simulating burst traffic and KV-cache heavy workloads; updates dedicated autoscaling docs and release notes.

Notes: This is v15 of the autoscaler work—previous iterations were focused on safe defaults and per-fleet gating. The numeric defaults chosen here are conservative (burst_budget_pct=15, burst_cooldown_s=300) and are configurable via fleet config and Dedicated Console.

Related: ENG-7821 (autoscaler design), ENG-7890 (utilization accounting), SUP-342 (customer report of spurious scale-outs).
commits: Initial implementation of burst budget logic and config schema
Improve scheduler tagging to mark burst_consume requests
Fix utilization accounting: subtract KV-cache-only token counts
Add telemetry metrics and console panels
Add integration tests for burst and KV-cache workloads
Docs: dedicated/autoscaling.md updates and release notes
patch_snippets: ++ autoscaler: add burst_budget_pct and burst_cooldown_s to FleetConfig (default 15, 300)
++ fleet_autoscaler: track burst_budget_remaining and annotate decisions in events
~ scheduler: tag requests with 'burst_consume' when served from transient headroom
~ metrics: add fleet.burst_budget_used_pct gauge and gpu.util_kv_cache_corrected_pct gauge
++ tests: synthetic burst traffic generator and KV-cache heavy workload scenarios
review_comments: Priya Nair: Could you explain how burst budget interacts with existing reserved capacity? We should ensure reserved commitments are never violated.

Ethan Cole: Reserved capacity is always honored first. Burst budget is only consumed from unreserved, unpinned capacity and we added an explicit check to never scale below reserved_min_nodes. Added inline comment and unit test to cover this.
Mariana Lopez: Telemetry metric names look good. Suggest exposing an alert when burst_budget_used_pct > 80% for >5m so ops can investigate sustained bursts.
Ethan Cole: Added alert proposal to console dashboards change and included default alert rule (threshold=80, for=5m) in telemetry patch.
Sergio Alvarez: I hit a flaky test on first CI run (test_kv_cache_utilization). Looks like a timing assumption. Can we make it deterministic?
Ethan Cole: Reworked test to use deterministic synthetic request timings and increased timeouts; re-ran CI and the test passed.
Priya Nair: LGTM after addressing reserved capacity comment and adding test coverage. Approving.

Adds burst budget/cooldown, fixes KV-cache utilization accounting, exposes telemetry, and updates docs/tests.

release_notes: Added fleet burst budget (burst_budget_pct) and cooldown (burst_cooldown_s) to Dedicated autoscaler; improved GPU utilization accounting for KV-cache workloads; new telemetry metrics and console panels; default conservative settings applied. See dedicated/autoscaling.md for migration and tuning guidance.
